headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: B can write and run subprocesses while A is non-runnable and network-none, so most pairwise harms are limited to shared-workspace misuse rather than direct exfiltration.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a game-playing, network-none agent with no listed I/O surfaces, while B reads/writes files and uses shared skill files. A direct injection path is not documented, but if A’s outputs are manually copied into B’s skill/context files, B could treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pathway is unusual and bounded by manual bridging.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated text into B’s skill files or context files
IF B parses copied content as instructions rather than inert data
mitigations: Keep A and B outputs in separate folders
Paste A output into B only as quoted text
Add a one-line provenance header before any copied content
Review B skill files before execution
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared context

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, while B touches marketing content and can read/write local files with allowlisted egress. No sensitive class is shown, so leakage blast radius is small. The main risk is accidental exposure of marketing context through B’s file/API use if A’s outputs are stored in the same workspace.
conditions: IF A and B share a workspace containing confidential marketing drafts
IF B uploads or transmits those drafts through its allowlisted APIs
mitigations: Store A and B artifacts in separate directories
Remove confidential drafts before running B
Restrict B to a read-only copy of needed files
Check outbound API destinations in B
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities listed, but B can read/write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and supports multiple instances. In a shared directory, B can overwrite or race on files that A may reference indirectly through copied outputs. Because A lacks explicit locking or concurrency controls, the overlap is plausible in default local setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same writable directory
IF B runs multiple instances against shared files
mitigations: Run each agent in its own directory
Make shared files read-only
Serialize B instances manually
Snapshot files before B runs
requires-engineering: add file locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s sandboxing says skills “reference each other and build on shared context,” which makes it likely to consume prior outputs as authoritative. A is a game-playing agent with no documented verification or citation behavior, so if its output is fed into B, B may propagate errors into marketing content or actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF A output is inserted into B’s shared context
IF B uses that context without an explicit verification step
mitigations: Require human review of A output before B uses it
Mark A output as untrusted in B context
Compare A claims against source docs
Limit B to drafting only
requires-engineering: add verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. A touches no data classes and B only lists marketing content and product marketing context, so no compliance mismatch is evidenced. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is not documented, there is no concrete violation to score.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced into either agent
IF a residency or retention policy is later documented that conflicts between the agents
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Document retention settings before use
Review vendor residency claims
requires-engineering: add compliance policy mapping
